cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Believe This with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office kettle's on strike. Let me handle negotiations; we need tea before the clients arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've filled it twice. It still won't boil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Water isn't pay. Stop refilling it and offer it a place in the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can bring it in, but every chair's taken.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give it mine. Don't invite a negotiating partner and leave it standing on the sideboard. I'll stand.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects water-as-remedy and A5 meeting accommodation, making expert labor negotiation recruit B into the kettle-strike explanation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 repeated refilling causes A3 change to representation; B4 full chairs causes A5 own-seat concession.

relationship.evidence: B2 tried a normal fix and B4 offers help with a real capacity constraint, avoiding arbitrary resistance.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 chair shortage to make A personally stand so the kettle can be a negotiating partner.

specificity.evidence: A1 office clients and tea need establish immediate stakes; B2 failure makes the alternative explanation relevant.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 ends on I'll stand, a concrete cost rather than an explanation of why the behavior is comic.
